**Prerequisite:** Leadership sphere ((follower) package).

**Effect:** Followers may select advanced talents when selecting sphere options as part of their assistance, using their follower's skill ranks to meet associated skill rank prerequisites. For example, a blacksmith follower could now select the Artifice sphere Exceptional Equipment (flourish) talent.

In addition, each follower that could select a sphere option as part of their assistance may select 1 additional option this way (such as blacksmith now selecting 2 Artifice flourishes instead of 1, thanks to this feat and the talented followers legendary option).

**Normal:** A follower's assistance cannot select advanced talent options or options with prerequisites.

entries.name: Magician
entries.prerequisites: Leadership 5 associated skill ranks; Leadership ((follower) package).
entries.md:
**Prerequisites:** Leadership 5 associated skill ranks; Leadership ((follower) package).

**Effect:** You gain a talented magician as a follower. When you *make camp*, the magician establishes a place to perform their work - whether it is a makeshift wizard's tower, miniature cleric's temple, druid's standing stones, and so on - such that the magician can simulate their ideal surroundings.

When you first gain the services of a magician, choose a single spell list with access to 9th level spells (such as the wizard/sorcerer list, cleric list, druid list, witch list, and so on). You may choose a new spell list each time the magician would be replaced.

**Follower's Skill - Spellcraft:** The magician's Spellcraft bonus is equal to your associated skill bonus.

**Magician's Assistance:**

- *Magecraft*: Each day, the magician is able to cast a number of spell levels from their chosen spell list equal to your associated skill ranks (for example, with 8 associated skill ranks, the magician could cast 8 1st level spells, 4 2nd level spells, or any combination whose sum is 8). You must provide the magician with any expensive material components.

  The magician is treated as a prepared caster with access to their entire spell list (similar to a cleric or druid). The magician can cast up to 2nd level spells, +1 spell level per 4 associated skill ranks after 5th (having access to 3rd level spells at 9 associated ranks, 4th level at 13, and so on). Subject to GM discretion, certain spells may be limited from the magician in the same way a player character would be unable to access a spell, such as a magician being unable to cast *teleport* where long range teleportation is limited.
- *Magecraft, Prepared [plan] (requires 10 associated skill ranks)*: The magician can specially weave their magic so their spells become prepared as one of that creature's plans (even if that creature could not normally prepare a plan). A spell prepared this way takes effect when the plan is revealed and otherwise remains dormant. A creature may only have a total number of spell levels prepared through this assistance equal to half your associated skill ranks.

  The magician reduces the total number of spell levels they can cast using magecraft each day by the total number of spell levels prepared through this assistance.
- *Trinket Maintenance*: The magician can refill charges in staves and other similar rechargeable items, providing 1 charge to each such item per day (up to 1 + your practitioner modifier items). The magician cannot refill charges in a magic item that could not normally be refilled (such as being incapable of providing more charges to a *ring of three wishes*).

entries.name: Recruit Troop
entries.prerequisites: Leadership ((cohort) package).
entries.md:
**Prerequisite:** Leadership ((cohort) package).

**Effect:** When you *recruit* a cohort, you may instead *recruit* a troop that represents a group of like-minded, like-trained individuals in your service (referred to as the "**troop cohort**"). The troop cohort gains the troop subtype (*Bestiary 6*), modified as follows:

- **Troop Statistics:** A troop cohort determines their troop base damage using your associated skill ranks (not their Hit Dice).
- **Troop Attack:** A troop cohort deals its troop damage automatically, as normal. A troop can choose to instead make attacks, but cannot deal its automatic troop damage that round. When making an attack or attack action, the troop cohort uses its troop damage as its weapon damage.

  If the troop cohort would be equipped with ranged weapons, they do not deal their troop damage automatically and instead may attack a 10-foot square within their weapon's range, treating a single struck target as the target of their attack action (the same as using a scatter weapon).
- **Troop Equipment:** A troop cohort must be given 10 pieces of identical equipment to use that equipment.
- **Healing Troops:** A troop cohort can be healed by effects that target a single creature, but receive 1/2 the normal amount (minimum 1). If the effect could target multiple creatures, they receive the normal amount. Effects that heal an area restore half again as many hit points (+50%).

A troop cohort otherwise benefits from their job, as normal.

entries.name: Spymaster
entries.prerequisites: Leadership sphere 5 associated skill ranks; Leadership sphere (any 2 (follower) talents).
entries.md:
**Prerequisites:** Leadership sphere 5 associated skill ranks; Leadership sphere (any 2 (follower) talents).

**Effect:** You gain a talented spymaster as a follower. When you *make camp*, the spymaster coordinates your other followers, manages your network of contacts, and debriefs returning followers on your behalf.

**Follower's Skill - Diplomacy:** The spymaster's Diplomacy bonus is equal to your associated skill bonus.

**Spymaster's Assistance:**

- *Cover Story:* The spymaster spends 1 hour preparing a cover story for a creature, establishing a false persona including a spoofed alignment, identity, and job. A cover story provides a creature with a constant *nondetection* effect that also protects against mind-reading effects. If an effect attempts to bypass a cover story and fails, it instead returns information consistent with the cover story. A creature with a cover story may also use the spymaster's Diplomacy bonus in place of any Profession skill appropriate to their cover story. The spymaster may hand out a number of cover stories equal to 1, +1 per 10 associated skill ranks.

  The spymaster also provides cover stories to themselves and your other followers. Followers protected this way do not count against the total number of cover stories the spymaster may prepare.
- *Cover Story, Improved (requires 15 associated skill ranks):* Cover stories are impenetrable, always returning information relevant to the cover story. This does not mean a cover story cannot be foiled by mundane means, but simple magic to reveal or dig for information from a creature no longer bypasses a cover story.
- *Cutout:* If a follower needs to be replaced, you may replace that follower within 1 day rather than the normal 1 week, provided you are within 1 day's travel of a settlement. Whenever a follower is replaced, they forget all pertinent details about their travels with you, except that they still remember working for you, but cannot recall any details that could compromise you or your allies.
- *Handler:* For any follower whose assistance would cause them to leave camp, the spymaster may instead coordinate their trusted network to perform that assistance instead. This allows the assistance to be performed without the follower leaving camp, and the assistance is performed in 1/2 its usual time.

entries.name: Acolyte
entries.prerequisites: Advanced Cohorts (magic cohorts).
entries.md:
**Prerequisite:** Advanced Cohorts (magic cohorts).

**Ability Scores:** Str 8, Dex 13, Con 12, Int 10, Wis 15, Cha 14

**Saving Throws:** Fortitude (good), Reflex (bad), Will (good)

**Class Skills:** Knowledge (nature) (Int), Knowledge (planes) (Int), Perception (Wis), Spellcraft (Int), Survival (Wis), Use Magic Device (Cha), +2 class skills of the acolyte's choice

**Special:** An acolyte's base attack bonus is equal to 3/4 their cohort level.

An acolyte gains the following additional benefits at the listed levels:

- (1st level): The acolyte is a cohort caster. If the acolyte is a classic cohort caster, they select either the druid or shaman list as their spell list and use Wisdom as their casting modifier. If the acolyte is a spherecaster cohort, they gain either the Fate or the Nature sphere plus one additional sphere of their choice, and are treated as a High-Caster in each of these spheres.
- (2nd level): The acolyte gains a circumstance bonus equal to 1/2 their acolyte level on Knowledge (nature), Knowledge (planes), and Spellcraft checks.
- [**Acolyte's Spirit Connection**] (3rd level): The acolyte gains the shaman's spirit feature, treating their acolyte level as their shaman level for this purpose. At 3rd level, the acolyte gains the spirit ability of their chosen spirit, gaining the greater spirit ability at 9th level and true spirit ability at 15th level.
- [**Acolyte's Hex**] (5th level): The acolyte gains a single shaman hex, treating their acolyte level as their shaman level for this purpose. The acolyte must choose a hex from their chosen shaman spirit. At 11th level, the acolyte gains a second hex from their chosen spirit, and may now reselect one of these hexes each day after preparing their spells.

entries.name: Apprentice
entries.prerequisites: Advanced Cohorts (magic cohorts).
entries.md:
**Prerequisite:** Advanced Cohorts (magic cohorts).

**Ability Scores:** Str 10, Dex 14, Con 12, Int 15, Wis 13, Cha 8

**Saving Throws:** Fortitude (good), Reflex (good), Will (bad)

**Class Skills:** Craft (alchemy) (Int), Heal (Wis), Knowledge (arcana) (Int), Perception (Wis), Spellcraft (Int), +2 class skills of the apprentice's choice

**Special:** An apprentice's base attack bonus is equal to 3/4 their cohort level.

An apprentice gains the following additional benefits at the listed levels:

- (1st level): The apprentice is a cohort caster. If the apprentice is a classic cohort caster, they use the alchemist list as their spell list and Intelligence as their casting modifier. An apprentice must be a prepared caster, preparing their spells as extracts, the same as an alchemist. The apprentice gains the infusion discovery as a bonus alchemist discovery. If the apprentice is a spherecaster cohort, they gain either the Alteration or Enhancement sphere plus one additional sphere of their choice, and are treated as a High-Caster in each of these spheres. The apprentice may use the (instill) option for each sphere they possess, and cannot use a magic sphere ability without its (instill) option.
- (2nd level): The apprentice gains a circumstance bonus equal to 1/2 their apprentice level on Craft (alchemy), Heal, and Spellcraft checks.
- [**Apprentice's Discovery**] (3rd level): The apprentice gains a single alchemist discovery, treating their apprentice level as their alchemist level to determine the effects of and to qualify for alchemist discoveries, plus an additional alchemist discovery at 9th and 13th level.
- [**Brew Potion**] (5th level): The apprentice gains Brew Potion as a bonus feat. At 11th level, the apprentice may double the potion's gold cost to ignore a single spell prerequisite (but not any expensive material components or other required checks).

entries.name: Cutpurse
entries.md:
**Ability Scores:** Str 10, Dex 15, Con 12, Int 14, Wis 8, Cha 13

**Saving Throws:** Fortitude (bad), Reflex (good), Will (good)

**Class Skills:** Acrobatics (Dex), Bluff (Cha), Disable Device (Dex), Perception (Wis), Stealth (Dex), +2 class skills of the cutpurse's choice

A cutpurse gains the following additional benefits at the listed levels:

- (1st level): The cutpurse gains the Equipment sphere Finesse Training talent and the Scoundrel sphere as a bonus sphere. If using *Spheres of Guile*, the cutpurse may exchange the Scoundrel sphere for the Infiltration or Subterfuge sphere.
- (2nd level): The cutpurse gains a circumstance bonus equal to 1/2 their cutpurse level on Disable Device and Stealth, as well as Perception checks made to avoid an ambush or notice traps. The cutpurse can disable magical traps. The cutpurse is treated as having the trap sense feature for the purpose of any feat or class prerequisite.
- [**Sneak Attack**] (3rd level): The cutpurse gains +1d6 sneak attack, +1d6 for every 4 cutpurse levels after 3rd level. This sneak attack functions as the unchained rogue's sneak attack class feature.
- [**Cutpurse Talents**] (5th level): The cutpurse gains a rogue talent, treating their cutpurse level as their rogue level to determine the effects of and to qualify for rogue talents, plus an additional rogue talent every 3 levels after 5th.

entries.name: Disciple
entries.md:
**Ability Scores:** Str 12, Dex 15, Con 13, Int 10, Wis 14, Cha 8

**Saving Throws:** Fortitude (good), Reflex (good), Will (bad)

**Class Skills:** Acrobatics (Dex), Escape Artist (Dex), Heal (Wis), Perception (Wis), Sense Motive (Wis), +2 class skills of the disciple's choice

A disciple gains the following additional benefits at the listed levels:

- (1st level): The disciple gains the Open Hand sphere and either the Equipment sphere Monk Weapon Training or Unarmed Weapon Training (discipline) talent. If using *Spheres of Guile*, the disciple may exchange the Open Hand sphere for the Body Control sphere.
- (2nd level): The disciple gains a circumstance bonus equal to 1/2 their disciple level on Acrobatics, Sense Motive, and Perception.
- [**Disciple's Flurry**] (3rd level): Whenever the disciple performs an attack action, the disciple may make an additional attack as a free action with a monk weapon or unarmed strike at a -2 penalty. At 11th level, the disciple may instead make two additional attacks, but both at a -4 penalty.

  The disciple treats this ability as the monk's flurry of blows class feature when performing an attack action, such as for the path of striking's benefits below or for other abilities and effects. The disciple does not receive additional attacks from other abilities or effects that grant benefits for possessing the flurry of blows feature (such as the Monk Weapon Training talent).
- [**Disciple's Path**] (5th level): The disciple chooses either the path of mysticism or the path of striking:
  - *Path of Mysticism*: The disciple gains the unchained monk's ki pool feature, treating their disciple level as their unchained monk level for this purpose and to determine the effects of and to qualify for ki powers. The disciple gains an unchained monk ki power, plus 1 additional ki power at 9th level and every 4 levels thereafter.
  - *Path of Striking*: The disciple gains the unchained monk's style strikes feature, treating their disciple level as their unchained monk level for this purpose. The additional attacks granted by the disciple's flurry feature are modified by the disciple's style strikes (or modifying two attacks at 15th level).

  If the disciple would use a style strike that requires another class feature, the disciple is treated as possessing that feature at its minimum bonus (such as, if performing the flying kick style strike, the disciple would be treated as having 10 feet of fast movement).

entries.name: Fortune Teller
entries.prerequisites: Advanced Cohorts (magic cohorts).
entries.md:
**Prerequisite:** Advanced Cohorts (magic cohorts).

**Ability Scores:** Str 8, Dex 12, Con 13, Int 14, Wis 10, Cha 15

**Saving Throws:** Fortitude (bad), Reflex (good), Will (good)

**Class Skills:** Knowledge (arcana) (Int), Knowledge (history) (Int), Perception (Wis), Spellcraft (Int), Use Magic Device (Cha), +2 class skills of the fortune teller's choice

**Special:** A fortune teller's base attack bonus is equal to 3/4 their cohort level.

A fortune teller gains the following additional benefits at the listed levels:

- **(1st level):** The fortune teller is a cohort caster. If the fortune teller is a classic cohort caster, they select either the psychic or witch spell list and Intelligence or Charisma as their casting modifier. If the fortune teller is a spherecaster cohort, they receive the Divination or Mind sphere as a bonus sphere plus one additional sphere of their choice, and are treated as a High-Caster in each of these spheres.
- **(2nd level):** The fortune teller gains a circumstance bonus equal to 1/2 their fortune teller level on Knowledge (history), Spellcraft, and Use Magic Device checks.
- **[Fortune Teller's Implement] (3rd level):** The fortune teller gains the occultist mental focus feature with a number of points of mental focus equal to 1/2 their fortune teller level + their casting modifier. In addition, the fortune teller gains a single occultist implement, treating their fortune teller as their occultist level when determining the implement's resonant power and focus powers.
- **[Fortune Teller's Focus] (5th level):** The fortune teller gains a single focus power for their occultist implement, plus an additional focus power at 9th level and 13th level.

entries.name: Minstrel
entries.md:
**Ability Scores:** Str 8, Dex 15, Con 12, Int 14, Wis 10, Cha 13

**Saving Throws:** Fortitude (bad), Reflex (good), Will (good)

**Class Skills:** Diplomacy (Cha), Knowledge (history) (Int), Knowledge (nobility) (Int), Perception (Wis), Perform (any) (Cha), +2 class skills of the minstrel's choice

A minstrel gains the following additional benefits at the listed levels:

- (1st level): The minstrel gains Cunning and Skill Focus as bonus feats and the Warleader sphere with the music man drawback. If using *Spheres of Guile*, the minstrel may gain the Bluster or Performance sphere instead of the Warleader sphere.
- (2nd level): The minstrel gains a circumstance bonus equal to 1/2 their minstrel level on Knowledge (history), Knowledge (nobility), and all Perform checks. The minstrel may make Knowledge (history) and Knowledge (nobility) checks untrained.
- [**Minstrel's Performance**] (3rd level): The minstrel gains the bard's bardic performance feature, treating their minstrel level as their bard level for this purpose. The minstrel gains access to the countersong, distraction, fascinate, and inspire competence bardic performances. The minstrel does not gain any other bardic performances nor does the minstrel qualify for bardic masterpieces.
- [**Minstrel-of-All-Trades**] (5th level): The minstrel may take 10 on any skill check they are trained in, even if in immediate danger or distracted. Once per round, if another ally is benefitting from the minstrel's bardic performance, the minstrel may allow that ally to take 10 on a skill check, even if in immediate danger or distracted, provided that the ally is trained in that skill.

entries.name: Naturalist
entries.md:
**Ability Scores:** Str 13, Dex 15, Con 12, Int 10, Wis 14, Cha 8

**Saving Throws:** Fortitude (good), Reflex (good), Will (bad)

**Class Skills:** Handle Animal (Cha), Heal (Wis), Knowledge (nature) (Int), Perception (Wis), Survival (Wis), +2 class skills of the naturalist's choice

A naturalist gains the following additional benefits at the listed levels:

- (1st level): The naturalist gains the Alchemy sphere as a bonus sphere and a single Equipment sphere (discipline) talent of their choice. If using *Spheres of Guile*, the naturalist may gain the Herbalism sphere instead of the Alchemy sphere.
- (2nd level): The naturalist gains a circumstance bonus equal to 1/2 their naturalist level on Craft (alchemy), Heal, and Survival. If the naturalist selected a different associated skill for the Alchemy or Herbalism spheres, they may choose to exchange one of these skills for that skill (the new skill should still be appropriate for a naturalist cohort, subject to GM discretion).
- [**Naturalist's Enemy**] (3rd level): The naturalist gains a single favored enemy, as the ranger's favored enemy feature, with a +2 favored enemy bonus. The naturalist can change their favored enemy selection once per day with 1 hour of preparation.

  At 11th level, the naturalist's favored enemy bonus increases to +4. The naturalist does not select an additional favored enemy.
- [**Naturalist Specialty**] (5th level): The naturalist chooses either the hunter specialty or the traveler's specialty:
  - *Hunter's Specialty*: As a move action, the naturalist may make a single Knowledge check to identify a creature they can see, gaining a circumstance bonus on this check equal to 1/2 the naturalist's level. This Knowledge check may be made even if untrained. On a success, the naturalist may treat the target as though they were their favored enemy for 1 minute. If the target is already the naturalist's favored enemy, the naturalist deals an additional +1d6 precision damage on weapon attacks against the target. At 9th level, the naturalist may now use this ability as a move or swift action. At 13th level, the bonus precision damage improves to +2d6 and the naturalist always receives this bonus damage, even if the target is not the naturalist's favored enemy.
  - *Traveler's Specialty*: The naturalist gains the ranger's woodland stride feature and selects a single favored terrain, as the ranger's favored terrain feature. The naturalist may reselect their favored terrain once per week. At 9th level, the naturalist may move unimpeded through any terrain, natural or magical. At 13th level, once per day, the naturalist may share this traveler's specialty with a number of creatures within 30 feet equal to 1/2 their naturalist level; this benefit lasts for 1 minute per naturalist level.

entries.name: Priest
entries.prerequisites: Advanced Cohorts (magic cohorts).
entries.md:
**Prerequisite:** Advanced Cohorts (magic cohorts).

**Ability Scores:** Str 13, Dex 10, Con 12, Int 8, Wis 15, Cha 14

**Saving Throws:** Fortitude (good), Reflex (bad), Will (good)

**Class Skills:** Heal (Wis), Knowledge (religion) (Int), Perception (Wis), Sense Motive (Wis), Spellcraft (Int), Use Magic Device (Cha), +2 class skills of the priest's choice

**Special:** A priest's base attack bonus is equal to 3/4 their cohort level.

A priest gains the following additional benefits at the listed levels:

- **[Priestly Worship] (1st level):** The priest worships a deity or other source that could grant a cleric spells. A priest must be within 1 step of their deity's alignment and they must channel energy as a cleric appropriate to their deity.
- **(1st level):** The priest is a cohort caster. If the priest is a classic cohort caster, they use the cleric spell list and Wisdom or Charisma as their casting modifier. If the priest is a spherecaster cohort, they gain a bonus magic talent from a sphere associated with one of their deity's domain (as a sphere cleric) and either the Life sphere or the Death sphere based on whether they channel positive or negative energy respectively, and are treated as a High-Caster in each of these spheres.
- **(2nd level):** The priest gains a circumstance bonus equal to 1/2 their priest level on Heal, Knowledge (religion), and Sense Motive checks.
- **[Priest's Domain] (3rd level):** The priest selects a single cleric domain, treating their priest level as their cleric level for this purpose. If the priest is a classic cohort caster, the priest may prepare domain spells or select them as spells known as though they were on the cleric spell list. If the priest is a spherecaster cohort, the priest gains a bonus magic talent from a sphere associated with their domain.
- **[Channel Energy] (5th level):** The priest gains the channel energy class feature, channeling either positive or negative energy based on their selection for priestly worship. The priest's channel energy is equal to 1d6 per 3 priest levels, and they may channel energy a number of times per day equal to 1 + their casting modifier.

entries.name: Squire
entries.md:
**Ability Scores:** Str 14, Dex 12, Con 15, Int 10, Wis 13, Cha 8

**Saving Throws:** Fortitude (good), Reflex (good), Will (bad)

**Class Skills:** Diplomacy (Cha), Handle Animal (Cha), Knowledge (nobility) (Int), Ride (Dex), Sense Motive (Wis), +2 class skills of the squire's choice

A squire gains the following additional benefits at the listed levels:

- (1st level): The squire gains the Guardian sphere and an additional Equipment sphere talent of their choice. If using *Spheres of Guile*, the squire may gain the Artifice sphere instead of the Guardian sphere, and must select the gear package.
- (2nd level): The squire gains a circumstance bonus equal to 1/2 their squire level on all Diplomacy, Handle Animal, Knowledge (nobility), and Ride checks. The squire can make Knowledge (nobility) checks even if untrained.
- [**Squire's Order**] (3rd level): The squire gains a cavalier order, including its order benefits, challenge bonus, skill bonus, and order abilities, treating their squire level as their cavalier level for this purpose.

  If the squire possesses the Guardian (challenge) package, their order's challenge bonus applies against a target affected by their Guardian *challenge*. If the squire possesses the Guardian (patrol) package, their order's challenge bonus applies on attacks of opportunity made as part of their *patrol*.
- [**Aide de Camp**] (5th level): The squire is uniquely adept at assisting their leader. The squire gains Quick Draw as a bonus feat, and can retrieve any kind of equipment or item from their person using the Quick Draw feat, not just weapons. When within reach, the squire or leader may retrieve items from one another as a free action (or items may be handed to one another as a free action, provided the other has a free hand to receive it).

  This does not allow the squire or their leader to retrieve items that are inside containers faster, but would allow the leader to take a readied polearm from their squire as they advance on the enemy.

entries.name: Student
entries.prerequisites: Advanced Cohorts (magic cohorts).
entries.md:
**Prerequisite:** Advanced Cohorts (magic cohorts).

**Ability Scores:** Str 10, Dex 12, Con 13, Int 15, Wis 14, Cha 8

**Saving Throws:** Fortitude (bad), Reflex (good), Will (good)

**Class Skills:** Knowledge (arcana) (Int), Knowledge (any one) (Int), Perception (Wis), Spellcraft (Int), Use Magic Device (Cha), +2 class skills of the student's choice

**Special:** A student's base attack bonus is equal to 3/4 their cohort level.

A student gains the following additional benefits at the listed levels:

- **(1st level):** The student is a cohort caster. If the student is a classic cohort caster, they use the wizard spell list and Intelligence as their casting modifier, preparing their spells from a spellbook. If the student is a spherecaster cohort, they receive any two magic spheres as bonus spheres, and are treated as a Mid-Caster.
- **(2nd level):** The student gains a circumstance bonus equal to 1/2 their student level on Knowledge (arcana), Spellcraft, and Use Magic Device checks.
- **[Arcane School] (3rd level):** The student selects a single arcane school, treating their student level as their wizard level for this purpose.
- **[Student's Scrolls] (5th level):** The student gains Scribe Scroll as a bonus feat. At 11th level, the student may double the scroll's gold cost to ignore a single spell prerequisite (but not any expensive material components or other required checks).

entries.name: Warrior
entries.md:
**Ability Scores:** Str 15, Dex 14, Con 12, Int 13, Wis 10, Cha 8

**Saving Throws:** Fortitude (good), Reflex (bad), Will (good)

**Class Skills:** Climb (Str), Knowledge (dungeoneering) (Int), Perception (Wis), Profession (soldier), Swim (Str), +2 class skills of the warrior's choice

A warrior gains the following additional benefits at the listed levels:

- (1st level): The warrior gains the Equipment sphere Armor Training talent and an additional Equipment sphere (discipline) talent of their choice. In addition, a warrior may qualify for feats as though they were a fighter, treating their warrior level as their fighter level for this purpose.
- (2nd level): The warrior gains a circumstance bonus equal to 1/2 their warrior level on all Strength-based skill checks, Intimidate, and Knowledge (dungoneering). The warrior can make Knowledge (dungeoneering) checks even if untrained.
- [**Armor Experience**] (3rd level): The warrior gains the fighter's armor training feature, treating their warrior level as their fighter level for this purpose.
- [**Weapon Experience**] (5th level): The warrior chooses a (discipline) talent (except Custom Training). The warrior gains a +1 bonus on attack and damage rolls with weapons belonging to the chosen (discipline). This bonus improves by an additional +1 every 4 levels after 5th. The warrior is treated as having the fighter's weapon training feature, and treats their weapon experience bonus as their weapon training bonus for this purpose.

entries.name: Wildling
entries.md:
**Ability Scores:** Str 15, Dex 12, Con 14, Int 10, Wis 13, Cha 8

**Saving Throws:** Fortitude (good), Reflex (good), Will (bad)

**Class Skills:** Climb (Str), Knowledge (nature) (Int), Perception (Wis), Survival (Wis), Swim (Str), +2 class skills of the wildling's choice

A wildling gains the following additional benefits at the listed levels:

- (1st level): The wildling gains Endurance and Toughness as bonus feats and the Berserker sphere as a bonus sphere. If using *Spheres of Guile*, the wildling may gain the Survivalism sphere instead of the Berserker sphere.
- (2nd level): The wildling gains a circumstance bonus equal to 1/2 their wildling level on Knowledge (nature), Perception, and Survival. The wildling can make Knowledge (nature) checks even if untrained.
- [**Wildling Rage**] (3rd level): The wildling can rage as the barbarian's rage feature, treating their wildling level as their barbarian level for this purpose. When the wildling first gains the rage feature this way, they must choose whether their rage functions as a barbarian's or an unchained barbarian's rage.

  At 11th level, the wildling gains the greater rage feature.
- [**Totemic Rage**] (5th level): The wildling gains a single blood or totem rage power, treating their wildling level as their barbarian level to determine the effects of and to qualify for rage powers. The wildling gains their selected blood or totem rage power's improvement at 9th level and again at 13th level.

entries.name: Drill Sergeant
entries.prerequisites: (cohort) package.
entries.md:
**Prerequisite:** (cohort) package.

You cannot *recruit* cohorts and can only be the leader of conscripted allies (using the temporary conscription option). You gain Temporary Conscription and 1 other (cohort) talent of your choice.

**Incompatible:** Strange Bedfellows.

entries.name: Established Footprint
entries.prerequisites: (follower) package.
entries.md:
Your camp is a more elaborate guild hall, office, or other establishment that cannot be moved so simply.

**Prerequisite:** (follower) package.

You must *make camp* in a settlement, and it takes 1 week to *make camp*. You gain a (follower) talent as a bonus talent.

entries.name: Strange Bedfellows
entries.prerequisites: (cohort) package.
entries.md:
**Prerequisite:** (cohort) package.

Choose one exotic cohort type offered by the Exotic Cohort legendary talent. You gain Exotic Cohort as a bonus talent and can only *recruit* cohorts with the chosen exotic cohort type.

**Note:** This drawback offers the benefits of a legendary talent and should only be available subject to GM discretion.

**Incompatible:** Drill Sergeant.

entries.name: Wicked Tyrant
entries.md:
Instead of selecting an associated skill, you gain Intimidate as your associated skill for this sphere. With this alternate start, you lead your cohorts and followers using fear, and as such, cannot maintain contacts. Subject to GM discretion, the allies, family, and friends of *recruited* cohorts may also withhold services or refuse to interact with you (especially if the cohort was mistreated or killed in your service).

If using the optional rule **Associated Skill Checks to *Recruit* Cohorts**, you do not suffer any penalties to *recruit* a cohort due to mistreatment or cohort death.

---

*Archived: [[Leadership Sphere Drawbacks (Ultimate)|Ultimate version]] (before *Polished*)*

entries.name: Camp of Operations
entries.prerequisites: Leadership 3 associated skill ranks; Leadership sphere ((follower) package); base of operations class feature.
entries.md:
*Source: [Polished Leadership](https://www.drivethrurpg.com/en/product/585162/diamond-polished-spheres-leadership-sphere)*

*Home is wherever the hearth is.*

**Prerequisites:** Leadership 3 associated skill ranks; Leadership sphere ((follower) package); base of operations class feature.

**Benefit:** Whenever you establish a base of operations, you may also *make camp*.

In addition, your base of operations gains 1 additional tailored advice benefit. An additional benefit added this way is chosen based on the sphere-related assistance your followers offer, not the base spheres you personally possess (such as selecting Artifice's base of operations benefit by having a blacksmith, whose assistance offers Artifice sphere effects, despite not having the Artifice sphere normally).

**Note:** The base of operations feature was first printed with the advisor class, *Diamond Spheres: Harmony and Discord*.

entries.name: Emergency Reserves
entries.prerequisites: Leadership 5 associated skill ranks; Leadership ((cohort) package).
entries.md:
*Source: [Polished Leadership](https://www.drivethrurpg.com/en/product/585162/diamond-polished-spheres-leadership-sphere)*

*You can make preparations for a new cohort should your current cohort die or need to be replaced.*

**Prerequisite:** Leadership 5 associated skill ranks; Leadership ((cohort) package).

**Benefit:** You gain the following plan:

> **Emergency Reserves [plan]**
>
> **Effect:** When you prepare this plan, you must still spend the time to recruit, determining the cohort's statistics and abilities, but gaining that cohort as a contact instead of immediately gaining their services.
>
> When you reveal this plan, the prepared cohort arrives in 15 minutes, as though just recruited. You may only reveal this plan if you have an available slot for a cohort (such as a cohort having recently died or needing replacement). This plan may only be prepared a single time, even if you could prepare multiple plans at once.

entries.name: Friends In Close Places
entries.prerequisites: Leadership sphere 10 associated skill ranks; Leadership sphere (2 (follower) talents).
entries.md:
*Source: [Polished Leadership](https://www.drivethrurpg.com/en/product/585162/diamond-polished-spheres-leadership-sphere)*

*Your retinue of followers has attracted some skilled individuals you can call on in a time of need.*

**Prerequisites:** Leadership sphere 10 associated skill ranks; Leadership sphere (2 (follower) talents).

**Benefit:** You gain a single Leadership sphere (follower) talent as a bonus talent. In addition, you gain the following plan:

> **Friends in Close Places [plan]**
>
> **Effect:** When you reveal this plan, you immediately retrain the (follower) talent granted by this feat. This is treated as dismissing one follower to gain the services of another, with the new follower arriving the next time you *make camp*. Any assistance provided by a follower is lost when that follower is dismissed (provided items become inert and useless, abilities or benefits end, and so on).
>
> If you are in a settlement, you may reveal this plan once per day. Otherwise, you may only reveal this plan once per week or until you make camp in a settlement.

entries.name: Journeyman Cohorts
entries.prerequisites: Leadership sphere 3 associated skill ranks; Leadership sphere ((cohort) package).
entries.md:
*Source: [Polished Leadership](https://www.drivethrurpg.com/en/product/585162/diamond-polished-spheres-leadership-sphere)*

**Prerequisite:** Leadership sphere 3 associated skill ranks; Leadership sphere ((cohort) package).

**Effect:** Each cohort you *recruit* also selects one cohort job they do not possess, gaining that job's 2nd-level benefit and their choice between that job's 3rd and 5th-level benefits. For example, a wildling could select warrior, gaining their 2nd-level skill bonuses and their choice between armor or weapon training.

Additional job benefits granted by this feat can be retrained similar to retraining a feat, such as with Training Coordination's training regiment option.

entries.name: Mixed Conscription
entries.prerequisites: Leadership sphere 5 associated skill ranks; ability to control one or more non-Leadership sphere subordinates (see text).
entries.md:
*Source: [Polished Leadership](https://www.drivethrurpg.com/en/product/585162/diamond-polished-spheres-leadership-sphere)*

**Prerequisites:** Leadership sphere 5 associated skill ranks; ability to control one or more non-Leadership sphere subordinates (see text).

**Benefit:** Other subordinates under your control are treated as one of your cohorts, and you are treated as their leader.

A subordinate may now benefit from (cohort) talents, except those that permanently improve or modify a cohort, such as quartermaster's skill, talented cohorts, and training regiment. Class features or other abilities that further customize cohorts similarly do not apply to subordinates (such as a knight captain's squires or a sheriff's deputies).

entries.name: Mixed Coordinator
entries.prerequisites: Beastmastery sphere, (handle animal) package, Leadership sphere, (cohort) package.
entries.md:
**Prerequisites:** Beastmastery sphere, (handle animal) package, Leadership sphere, (cohort) package.

When you tame a creature or recruit a cohort, you may choose to have its Hit Dice count against both your tame and recruit limits. When doing so, the creature counts as both an animal ally and a cohort for the purpose of talents that grant actions to or are triggered by cohorts and animal allies.

entries.name: Radiant Quests
entries.prerequisites: Leadership associated skill 5 ranks.
entries.md:
*Source: [Polished Leadership](https://www.drivethrurpg.com/en/product/585162/diamond-polished-spheres-leadership-sphere)*

*Not every job needs a sword. Some just need someone willing to ask around.*

**Prerequisites:** Leadership associated skill 5 ranks.

**Benefits:** Once per week, you can complete various tasks for your contacts or followers to make money. Make a Leadership sphere associated skill check, earning a number of gold pieces equal to your check's result times your associated skill ranks. You can only complete a radiant quest once per week.

When completing a radiant quest on behalf of a contact or follower, you must spend 8 hours working towards their radiant quest (similar to working a profession or spending downtime to make money). A radiant quest typically involves a negligible amount of combat, exploration, and travel, which you are considered to have succeeded on during the downtime.

When you complete a radiant quest for a contact, if that contact is *recruited* as a cohort within 1 week, they gain a +2 morale bonus to attack rolls, damage rolls, saving throws, and skill checks for 48 hours.

When you complete a radiant quest for a follower, for the next 48 hours, that follower provides their assistance as though your Leadership sphere associated skill ranks and practitioner modifier were 2 higher.

entries.name: Shared Harmonies
entries.prerequisites: Leadership sphere ((cohort) package); bardic performance or raging song class feature.
entries.md:
*Source: [Polished Leadership](https://www.drivethrurpg.com/en/product/585162/diamond-polished-spheres-leadership-sphere)*

*Songs are better sung with two voices.*

**Prerequisites:** Leadership sphere ((cohort) package); bardic performance or raging song class feature.

**Benefit:** You gain the following abilities:

- **Pass the Song:** When you begin or continue your bardic performance or raging song, as a free action, you may allow a cohort within close range (25 ft. + 5 ft. / 2 Leadership associated skill ranks) to continue performing the performance or song on your behalf. The cohort may maintain the performance or song as a standard action each round, and expends your rounds of bardic performance or raging song to do so.

  You can begin new bardic performances or raging songs while a cohort maintains your previous performance or song; multiple instances of the same performance or song do not stack.
- **Start a Harmony:** When you begin your bardic performance or raging song, your cohort may harmonize with you as a joint standard action. Each round the cohort harmonizes with you, or continues to harmonize each round after the first as a standard action, you treat the effects of your bardic performance or raging song as though your class level were 6 higher to determine its effects.

  A cohort cannot harmonize with you after you've begun your performance or song, and only a single cohort can harmonize this way.

**Special - Minstrel Cohorts (see text):** If your cohort possesses the bardic performance or raging song class feature, they may select this feat as though they met the prerequisites. When the cohort uses their bardic performance or raging song, you or other cohorts may harmonize with them.

**Special - Bardic Performance-like features:** Subject to GM discretion, class features that function similar to bardic performance (such as symbiat's psionics) may be used with this feat, and may be used to meet this feat's prerequisites.

entries.name: Shared Rage
entries.prerequisites: Leadership sphere ((cohort) package); rage or bloodrage class feature, or other ability to rage (see text).
entries.md:
*Source: [Polished Leadership](https://www.drivethrurpg.com/en/product/585162/diamond-polished-spheres-leadership-sphere)*

*Sharing your feelings never smashed so many helmets.*

**Prerequisites:** Leadership sphere ((cohort) package); rage or bloodrage class feature, or other ability to rage (see text).

**Benefit:** Whenever you rage, as a joint swift action, cohorts within close range (25 ft. + 5 ft. / 2 Leadership associated skill ranks) may also begin raging as a "**shared rage**", gaining all the benefits and penalties of rage, except the shared rage's benefits are half your normal rage's benefits (i.e. if your rage would grant +4 Strength and Constitution, the cohort only gains +2 Strength and Constitution). A cohort can rage indefinitely, so long as you are raging, and becomes fatigued for a duration when they stop raging.

You may choose to allow a cohort's shared rage to benefit from your full rage benefits (instead of half); however, if you do, each round the cohort spends raging expends your rounds of rage. If you rage due to a spell or similar effect with a fixed duration, the cohort instead expends time from that effect's total duration (such as reducing a *rage* spell's duration by an additional round).

**Special - Wildling Cohorts (see text):** If your cohort possesses the rage class feature, they may select this feat as though they met the prerequisites. When the cohort rages, you may enter a shared rage with them.

entries.name: Talented Followers, Improved
entries.prerequisites: Leadership sphere 5 associated skill ranks; Leadership ((follower) package, Good Help).
entries.md:
*Source: [Polished Leadership](https://www.drivethrurpg.com/en/product/585162/diamond-polished-spheres-leadership-sphere)*

*It's almost like they could do this all without me.*

**Prerequisites:** Leadership sphere 5 associated skill ranks; Leadership ((follower) package, Good Help).

**Benefit:** Followers can select 1 additional sphere option as part of their assistance (such as a blacksmith now selecting 3 Artifice flourishes instead of 2, thanks to the talented followers legendary option and this feat).

**Special:** This feat may be selected an additional time at 10 Hit Dice and every 5 additional Hit Dice after; each time this feat is selected, your followers select 1 additional option.

entries.name: Theurgical Disciples
entries.prerequisites: Leadership ((cohort) package); domain or inquisition class feature, cohort same alignment as you (see text).
entries.md:
*Source: [Polished Leadership](https://www.drivethrurpg.com/en/product/585162/diamond-polished-spheres-leadership-sphere)*

*Faith is strongest when kneeling before the same altar.*

**Prerequisite:** Leadership ((cohort) package); domain or inquisition class feature, cohort same alignment as you (see text).

**Benefit:** You gain a +2 bonus to Knowledge (religion) skill checks. If you have 10 or more ranks in Knowledge (religion), this bonus increases to +4.

In addition, each cohort that shares an alignment with you and that worships the same deity as you gains access to a single domain or inquisition that could be granted by your deity's portfolio. Cohorts use their cohort level as their effective cleric level when determining the domain or inquisition's effects.
